### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via getTypes (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getTypes, bound to GET /api/v1/meta), meta.getTypes (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/meta))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation), METADATA_CONFLICT (literal, a string literal in handlePermissionSetCloneWrite))_
- `content/docs/deployment/validating-metadata.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`  _(via saveMetaItem (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handlePermissionSetCloneWrite (symbol, a top-level function))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via METADATA_CONFLICT (literal, a string literal in handlePermissionSetCloneWrite))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `/api/v1/meta (route, 39 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **147** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b80204e187d996f001fdd99c48d33074115fcafd` — the merge of head `26a5eb92cc60a50d12b7b185ccfe536394d37f2c` into base `e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b80204e187d996f001fdd99c48d33074115fcafd && git checkout b80204e187d996f001fdd99c48d33074115fcafd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d 26a5eb92cc60a50d12b7b185ccfe536394d37f2c && git checkout -B drift-repro e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d && git merge --no-ff 26a5eb92cc60a50d12b7b185ccfe536394d37f2c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-15T07:04Z

This is the seat review of record for #23577 (claim `6185014283`, ruling `6184789291` letter B) on head:

`f0761ed3` (`9ec5053e`, the REST-pin fix `3f354c73`, and one changeset-only commit from this seat's patch round)

It is not the contract review. That review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, because the spec docblock hunk is published schema prose (ruling item 3).

1. **Form.**
   - Draft to `main`. The first line is `Fixes #23577`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at the start of a line.
   - 15 files, +335/−345. Not governed: `check-governed-merges --pr 23626` hits 0 of 15 paths, 680 changed lines.
   - Patch changesets for `metadata-protocol`, `runtime` and `spec`. No `content/docs/releases/` change.
2. **Against the ruling, item by item.**
   - **Item 1.** Every write over a sealed, package-held name on a type with no regime row reads `'TYPE/NAME' is provided by a managed package and is sealed: it cannot be written here. GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE lists the names in use.` (`packaged-base-regime.ts`, verbatim the ruling's text).
     - It holds at the protocol door and at the repository's type door.
     - There is no create advice and no source-artifact advice.
     - The package is not named. The dev measured that neither door has it at hand (`isSealedManagedItem` is a boolean), so no lookup is added.
     - Code `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` and status `403` are unchanged.
   - **Item 2.** `sealedWrite`, the `'create'` member of `packagedBaseRefusal` and `SealedItemOperation`'s `create` arm retire.
     - `SealedItemOperation` is not exported. The two public methods' parameters narrow, and the changeset names them.
     - The `version` and `currentVersion` describes say a `null` beside `editable: false` takes no save and prescribe no pin. `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` was regenerated by the generator.
   - **Item 3.** Position 2: the stale `## create` docblock is replaced. Position 3: the clone door rethrows a lost race as its own name-taken `409` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, with no `If-Match`. The `/meta` door's conflict sentence for its own callers is unchanged.
   - **Item 4.** These requests all read the one sentence on both kernel shapes: console create (draft + `*`), publish `*`, unpinned draft, unpinned and pinned. A `view` first write pinned `*` still lands an overlay row. #23565's two pins, the protocol one and the REST one, are re-pointed.
3. **Hypotheses measured** (the dev's report `6186403427`): no `packages/spec` schema declares an `operation` detail (H1); the export surface (H2); the package is not at hand (H3); where the clone's 409 is built (H4); the overlay path (H5); the regenerated outputs (H6).
4. **Gates.**
   - Locally on `9ec5053e`: 122 derived families, 121 run, 1 NOT MEASURED (shallow clone).
   - Two real reds on the first run (`check:durability-log-level`, `check:engine-double-contract`) were fixed in `9ec5053e`.
   - Two ablations were run, each red as predicted and restored.
   - CI on `9ec5053e`: Test Core 5/6 was red on `rest-meta-sealed-first-draft-remedy.test.ts`, #23565's REST pin of the retired split. It was re-pointed in `3f354c73`; the file and its neighbour pass 6/6.
   - CI on `3f354c73` was cancelled by the next push. CI on `f0761ed3` is converging, and landing waits on every check.
5. **Patch round (this seat): release text.**
   - `.changeset/23406-sealed-first-draft-remedy.md` is unconsumed and in the same release. It stated the draft/publish split this PR retires, and this PR's changeset answered it with a "supersedes" erratum.
   - `AGENTS.md` (the `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` row) says a falsified entry is amended in itself, never by an erratum in a later one. So `f0761ed3` drops the split from the 23406 entry, which keeps its first-write-pin `409` sentence, and deletes the erratum.
   - This seat also amended the PR body through the relay: the re-pointed REST pin, the 5/6 red and its fix, and this changeset round.
6. **Accepted deviations.** The model-free commit trailers (AGENTS.md). The PR body could not be edited by the dev: there is no relay op for it, so the seat did it.
7. **The dev's open questions.**
   - **Q1, regime types (`flow`, `action`, `permission`, `datasource`): A.** They keep their regime sentences. ADR-0126 §2 binds those sentences, and they carry neither create nor source-artifact advice, which is what the ruling's sentence removes. If the maintainer reads item 1 more widely, that is a follow-up, not this PR's.
   - **Q2, the `ITEM_LOCKED` named-base limb, which still says "Edit the source artifact and redeploy": noted, not filed.** It has a different code, and no producer of a named read-only-base write was measured. It goes in this seat's ledger. Dedupe words: `readOnlyBaseOverrideError ITEM_LOCKED source artifact redeploy`.
   - **Q3, the 23406 changeset: B**, done in item 5 above.
8. **Landing terms.** First a contract review PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the head, then every check green. Then the seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge. On merge #23577 closes, and its `pm:*` labels leave in the same act. `needs:contract-review` stays on this PR until the review passes.

## Pending release note corrected — maintainer confirmation needed · `domain:spec` seat 2 · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-15T07:07Z

`Check Changeset` step 12 is red on `f0761ed3`, in the **deliberate correction** class that `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs` names. It is not a collision. The gate stays red by design until a person confirms, so this PR cannot enter the merge queue on its own. That is why `needs-user-decision` is on it.

- **The note:** `.changeset/23406-sealed-first-draft-remedy.md`. It is unconsumed, from PR #23565 (#23406), and ships in the same release as this PR.
- **What changed under it:**
  - The note said a first draft over a sealed item "is told to edit the source artifact, not to choose another name", and that a publish-mode first write "still names a free name". That is the draft/publish remedy split.
  - Ruling `6184789291` (letter B) retires that split, and this PR implements it. At release every write over a sealed, package-held name reads one sentence, so both claims would ship false.
- **What this PR did to it (`f0761ed3`):**
  - It removed the split claims (the title's first clause, the "What was wrong" remedy paragraph, the first "What changed" bullet).
  - It kept the note's still-true half, the first-write-pin `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` sentence, and its "Unchanged" line.
  - This PR's own changeset carries no "supersedes" erratum. AGENTS.md's `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` row: a falsified entry is amended in itself, never by an erratum in a later one.
- **Restoring the note from base** would republish the false sentence, which the gate's text forbids for this class.

**Asked of the maintainer:** confirm this correction. With the contract review PASS and every other check green, the PR then lands by your merge. Alternatively, say "split", and the correction moves to its own docs-only PR while this one restores the note and lands through the queue.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f0761ed37b2bd86686fd433fe3db03570d206716`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-15T07:29Z by the contract reviewer for PR #23626 (card #23577, ruling 6184789291 letter B). Inputs: the card's body and its eleven comments, the PR's body and file list, the net diff of the head against its merge base `dd4ef38506` (15 files, +335/−345, equal to the PR's file list), and the check-runs on the head. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run; the head-side facts below were read with `git show` and `git grep` at the head.

Tier by face: `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts` is a published schema, so this is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, as the ruling's item 3 and the claim 6185014283 say. Governed surfaces: none of the 15 paths; Governed Surface Queue Guard is green. 680 changed lines, same-repo head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Request accept set at `PUT /api/v1/meta/:type/:name` and `saveMetaItem`: unchanged. Right.** The same requests are refused `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`; only the sentence moves. `packagedBaseRefusal` at the head branches on `'delete'` alone and sends every other operation to `refusePackagedBaseOverride`, which now builds `managedItemSealedSentence(type, name, 'save')`. Pinned at the protocol door (console create = draft + first-write pin, publish pin, unpinned draft, unpinned, pinned, on `position`, `object`, `flow`, both kernel shapes) and at the REST door (four requests, both kernels, `rest-meta-sealed-first-draft-remedy.test.ts` re-pointed in `3f354c73`). The overlay control (`view`, first write pinned `*`) lands one overlay row through the real write path over a stub engine.
2. **The row-less sentence is the ruled text verbatim. Right.** `'TYPE/NAME' is provided by a managed package and is sealed: it cannot be written here. GET /api/v1/meta/TYPE lists the names in use.` No create advice, no source-artifact advice, no hatch; 113 characters outside the name and type, pinned under the REST door's 500-character bound with an 88-character name on every row-less type. The registry enumeration holds every reachable row-less type (floor 15) and a plugin-registered type to it.
3. **Regime rows keep their sentences. Right, and ADR-bound.** `PACKAGED_BASE_REGIME` at the head holds exactly `flow`, `action`, `permission` (Regime C) and `datasource` (origin-gated), as the 23577 note states. ADR-0126 §2 D1 binds a Regime C refusal to name its sanctioned path; Prime Directive #13 makes that the ruling's ceiling, not the executor's. The enumeration pins that no regime sentence carries create advice and that no Regime C sentence carries source advice. See ③ for the dev's flag.
4. **Removals unchanged. Right.** The ruling's item 1 is about writes; the removal twin keeps its sentence, pinned.
5. **The holding package is not named. Right under the ruling's "at hand" clause.** `refusePackagedBaseOverride` asks `isSealedManagedItem`, a boolean over `isArtifactBacked`, which calls `lookupArtifactItem` and discards its result; the repository type door's seal limb (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:2136`) has only the caller-named base in scope. No lookup was added. Noted for the record, not as a defect: the artifact and its `_packageId` are computed one frame down and thrown away, so naming the package would be plumbing through two predicates, not a new lookup, if the maintainer ever wants it.
6. **Retirements. Right in substance; the declaration is the ② defect.** `sealedWrite` (a local), `heldNameSentence` (module-private) and the `create` arm of `SealedItemOperation` (not exported: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts` exports nothing from `packaged-base-regime.js`) are internal. But `packagedBaseRefusal`'s `operation` loses `'create'` and `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` loses its optional `operation`, and both are public methods of the exported class `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (published, in the Changesets `fixed` group). `'create'` shipped: `packages/metadata-protocol/CHANGELOG.md` under `## 18.0.0-next.0` (the #22591 entry, lines 955 to 970) records "The public input surface widens: `packagedBaseRefusal` accepts `operation: 'create'`, and `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` takes an optional operation", declared `Clause-②: yes`, graded `minor`. Its removal is the mirror act: a TypeScript consumer that passes `'create'` stops compiling; a JavaScript consumer that passes it reaches the override limb and reads the one sentence with the same code and status, so the runtime verdict does not move. The in-repo callers (`runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:1553`, `'save' | 'delete'`; `:1595`, no operation) are untouched and TypeScript Type Check is green.
7. **The repository type door reads the same builder. Right.** `override-artifact` intents (draft promotion, restore, revert) throw `managedItemSealedSentence(singular, name, operation)` with the same code and status; pinned in `package-writability.test.ts` and in objectql's `protocol-commit-history.test.ts` revert case.
8. **Spec: two `.describe()` texts, no key, no export, no shape. Right; `patch` for `@objectstack/spec` is right.** `GetMetaItemResponseSchema.version` and `MetadataConflictErrorSchema.currentVersion` now say a `null` beside `editable: false` takes no save and prescribe no pin for it, which is the ruling's item 2. The only generated output that moved is `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`, by exactly those two rows. H1 holds: `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` appears in `packages/spec/src` only as error-code-ledger rows and prose; no schema declares an `operation` detail, so the claim's stop-and-report condition did not arise.
9. **Clone door (position 3). Right; `patch` for `@objectstack/runtime` is right.** A `METADATA_CONFLICT` thrown by the create-only `saveMetaItem(parentVersion: null)` is rethrown as `nameTakenMessage(target.name)` with status 409 into the door's one `errorFromThrown`, which defaults `code` by status exactly as the step-5 name-taken path (`deps.error(message, 409)`) does, so the two refusals are byte-equal apart from the name; pinned (409, `RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, no `If-Match`, no `If-None-Match`). The `/meta` door's conflict sentence at `protocol.ts:19120` is untouched. The wire-visible change is on one race path only: `error.code` moves from `METADATA_CONFLICT` to `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and the sentence stops prescribing a header the door does not take. Wording want on the 23577 note, not a defect: name the old `METADATA_CONFLICT` code in the runtime bullet so an upgrading agent that greps it lands on the entry.
10. **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`: three rows for the new `view` control harness, written by the gate's `--write` path. Right;** Lint & Repo Gates is green on them.
11. **Position 2.** The `## create` section of `packagedBaseRefusal`'s docblock that named the retired position write-through is replaced by the one-`save` note. Right.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: no` is right.** No key on a published payload moves, which requests are accepted is unchanged, and the ruling binds it. The repo's own precedent for a narrowing with no payload key is the `c63028e` entry in this package's CHANGELOG: a `!` summary, `Clause-②: no`, and an ADR-0087 disposition marker. The Clause-② line is not where the breaking signal belongs here.
- **The `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` level and declaration are wrong.** The diff retires a released public input-surface member (judgment 6) and the changeset says nothing of it: no `**BREAKING**` line, no ADR-0087 disposition marker, graded `patch`. The repo's rule, recorded in `pr-automation.yml` under WHICH LEVEL from the maintainer's 2026-09-04 ruling: breaking-ness is carried by the `**BREAKING**` banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level, and in the launch window a breaking change grades `minor`; the same prerelease line already carries that form (the `OS_METADATA_WRITABLE` entry under `## 18.0.0-next.0`, "**BREAKING**, graded `minor` on the v18 prerelease line"). `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs`'s #13080 section names exactly this shape, a published type-surface narrowing that "declares **BREAKING** truthfully" because "a consumer's code can stop compiling", and names dropping the marker on it as the erosion the gate was rebuilt to stop. The changeset's "A caller that passed `operation: 'create'` passes `'save'`" is the migration line a breaking entry owes; it is not the declaration. So the changeset does not match what the diff publishes.
- **Remedy, one changeset-only commit on `.changeset/23577-sealed-write-one-sentence.md`:** grade `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor` (runtime and spec stay `patch`); add a `**BREAKING**` line that names the narrowing (the `'create'` member of `packagedBaseRefusal`'s `operation` and the `operation` parameter of `tenantAuthoredWriteRefusal` retire; a caller passes `'save'`; verdict, code and status unchanged, the text already there, now under the banner); and carry exactly one ADR-0087 disposition marker in the comment form the gate's header spells out. The gate prints the admissible categories when it refuses; by precedent (#8277's entry, and `c63028e` in this CHANGELOG) the fitting claim is `not-required (runtime-interface-only packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts#ObjectStackProtocolImplementation)`, a published runtime class, not a Zod projection, referenced by `packages/spec` only in prose, with a why that says no metadata, spec key, stored row or authorable spelling moves and the compiler is the channel. `type-surface-only` is not admissible: its predicate 4 admits a narrowing from `any`, `unknown` or no annotation only, and `'save' | 'create' | 'delete'` is a concrete union at the base. `Clause-②: no` stays. The 23406 amendment is unaffected. A fresh record on the new head is then owed; this one names `f0761ed3` only.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag 1, regime-row types: answered A, as implemented.** ADR-0126 §2 D1 binds the Regime C refusal to name its sanctioned path, and an accepted ADR binds until a superseding one says otherwise (Prime Directive #13); the ruling's fact base (presentation 6182970120 fact 2, the director's delta 6184655968) is the row-less pair, and the measured caller, the console's generic create on `position`, is row-less. The origin-gated `datasource` row names the source a code-defined item is declared in, and a code-defined item is not a package-held name, so it is outside item 1's wording. Reading item 1 across the regime rows would be an ADR-0126 amendment, a maintainer act, not this PR's.
- **Dev flag 2, the `ITEM_LOCKED` named-base limb: answered A for this PR.** The ruling binds the `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` refusal; `readOnlyBaseOverrideError` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:2250`) is a different code on a different condition, a caller that named a read-only base, where the package is at hand. Its "Edit the source artifact and redeploy" sends an installed package's administrator to an artifact they cannot edit, the defect class the ruling's facet ③ retired, so a follow-up card in the same family is warranted; the seat's "noted, not filed" is a Prime Directive #10 acceptance note that names its evidence, and filing is the seat's act. It conditions nothing here.
- **Dev flag 3, the 23406 note: B was taken in `f0761ed3`, and the correction is TRUE.** The amended entry keeps three claims and all three hold at the head: the first-write-pin `409 METADATA_CONFLICT` sentence ("this save asserted that no … row exists (the first-write pin, If-None-Match: * on the REST door), but one does") is at `protocol.ts:19120` and this diff does not touch it; the "What was wrong" paragraph describes the pre-#23565 text; the "Unchanged" line holds. The clauses it dropped (the draft/publish remedy split, "told to edit the source artifact", "still names a free name") would ship false after this PR. The entry is unconsumed (its text has zero hits in `packages/metadata-protocol/CHANGELOG.md`) and in the same release, so AGENTS.md's `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` row applies: amend the entry itself, never an erratum in a later one, and the 23577 note accordingly carries no "supersedes" line. The 23577 note states the release behaviour (one sentence, regime rows kept, the retired members, the clone door's 409) and is true at the head, subject to the ② declaration. **So the `Check Changeset` red on this head is the step-12 deliberate-correction refusal** (its annotation names `.changeset/23406-sealed-first-draft-remedy.md` with the two-class text), a decision for a person and not a defect of the diff; the PR comment 6186537521 and `needs-user-decision` carry it to the maintainer, `skip-changeset` is not applied (ruling D on #18375), and the context is not one of the five required ones. This record records the red as that decision.
- **PR body: one stale acceptance note.** "Unreleased changeset … This PR's changeset says so, and that file is not edited" contradicts the What changed bullet and the file list (`.changeset/23406-sealed-first-draft-remedy.md` is modified, 3/4).
